direction: Search de novo under imposed symmetry and only then break it: do not load the record except as a benchmark, and instead parametrise codes as orbits totalling 121 points under a subgroup $G$ of the signed-permutation group $B_8$ (generated programmatically from random even sign changes and coordinate permutations, choosing orbit sizes that sum to 121, e.g. one fixed point plus orbits of sizes 8, 16, or 32), optimise only the few orbit representatives with high-$\beta$ LogSumExp L-BFGS, seed additional families from the 240 $E_8$ roots by greedy max-min selection of 121 roots followed by swap moves, then gradually release the symmetry tying (representatives first move together, then all 121 points move freely) with LP polish at each release stage, retaining any released code whose contact graph differs from the record's.

idea: Deflated target-feasibility continuation on hinge loss with hole-grown and fresh starts plus Procrustes tabu, promoting distinct survivors to LogSumExp annealing and LP polish.
direction: Run a target-feasibility continuation in both threshold and point count, deflated away from the known basin: for targets $t=0.4600,0.4595,0.4590,\dots$ minimise the hinge loss $\sum_{i<j}\mathrm{relu}(\langle x_i,x_j\rangle-t)^2$ by Adam/L-BFGS from many fresh starts, including codes grown from optimised 115--120 point codes by inserting each new point at the numerically largest spherical hole (dense random sampling plus single-point refinement) and re-optimising all points, and add a tabu penalty that, after optimal orthogonal Procrustes alignment to the record configuration, penalises RMSD below $0.05$ so restarts cannot collapse back onto it; promote only the best few distinct survivors to full LogSumExp annealing and trust-region LP polish, and report the smallest feasible $t$ found.

idea: Walk out of the jammed LP vertex along equilibrium-stress-filtered floppy modes with geodesic line-search and re-polish to force a contact-topology change.
direction: Exploit rigidity and equilibrium-stress analysis to find a mechanism out of the LP vertex: assemble the tangent-space Jacobian $A$ of all pairs with slack $<10^{-5}$, solve the LP dual of the polish problem to obtain contact stresses $\lambda_{ij}\ge0$, discard zero-stress (redundant) contacts, and compute an SVD of the remaining $A$ to get its near-nullspace; take random combinations of null vectors with singular values below $10^{-6}$ as trial displacements, line-search along them on the sphere at angular steps $0.01$--$0.2$ rad while monitoring the true maximum and the number of contacts crossing slack $10^{-4}$, then re-polish with the LP at each step length, so the code deliberately walks along a floppy mode until second-order effects force a contact swap into a new topology.

idea: Rebalance the jammed contact graph with estimated symmetric pair stresses, then re-optimize with stress-inverse weighted LogSumExp plus contact-variance and frame-isotropy penalties that are gradually removed before final LP polish.
direction: Use stress-dual diagnostics to rebalance the jammed contact graph before re-polishing. From the incumbent, form contact sets at several tolerances, e.g. slack $<10^{-6},10^{-5},10^{-4}$, and solve for nonnegative pair stresses $w_{ij}$ satisfying, for every point $i$, $\sum_j w_{ij}P_i x_j=0$, where $P_i=I-x_ix_i^\top$, using a sparse LP or nonnegative least-squares formulation. Identify points with large equilibrium residual, near-zero total stress, or too few positively stressed contacts, and pairs carrying disproportionate stress; then run LogSumExp/Adam optimization at a deliberately relaxed level around $0.465$--$0.475$ with pair weights inversely related to their stresses, an added penalty on the variance of per-point stressed-contact counts, and a frame-isotropy penalty $\|XX^\top-(121/8)I\|_F^2$. Gradually remove these auxiliary penalties while lowering the target through $0.462$, $0.461$, and $0.460$, retain configurations whose stress residual and contact imbalance improve even if their cosine is initially slightly worse, and apply LP polish only during the final 20--30 seconds.

idea: Balanced overload/underload surgery alternating cap-cluster knockout with diverse void reinsertion plus joint hinge-to-LogSumExp annealing and LP polishing to force contact-topology changes.

Excise whole spectral contact-communities of 12-20 points plus adjacent low-degree outliers, refill holes by greedy search over 50000 sphere candidates, then subset-LogSumExp plus short all-point anneal over many seeds and LP-polish only distinct survivors.
direction: Perform macroscopic contact-community excision rather than removing one to five points. Build the contact graph using pairs within, say, $2\times10^{-5}$ of the maximum, detect communities with spectral clustering or greedy modularity, and in each trial remove an entire community of 12--20 points together with any adjacent low-contact outliers identified from the graph. Freeze the remaining points, generate at least 50,000 random sphere candidates, greedily place replacements in the largest holes with mutual separation enforced, then jointly optimize only the replacements against the frozen set using subset LogSumExp at increasing $\beta$, followed by a short all-point anneal. Run many time-boxed trials with different communities and random seeds, accept intermediates up to roughly $0.470$ provided their contact-graph Jaccard distance from the incumbent is below about $0.75$, and LP-polish only the two or three most topologically distinct survivors; this is intended to destroy hundreds of incumbent contacts simultaneously rather than letting removed points fall back into their original holes.

idea: Discrete E8/hypercube/rotated-union pool selection with greedy plus annealed swaps on precomputed Gram, then staged symmetry-breaking and LogSumExp L-BFGS release with LP polish under strict time budgets.
direction: Search from algebraic candidate pools instead of perturbing the record, while keeping the computation strictly time-boxed to avoid another timeout. Precompute Gram matrices for pools such as the 240 $E_8$ roots, the 128 normalized hypercube vertices $(\pm1,\ldots,\pm1)/\sqrt8$, 8D cross-polytope-derived points, and several random rotations/unions of these pools; use greedy insertion plus simulated-annealing swaps to select 121 pool points minimizing a smooth maximum of their pairwise cosines, updating swap costs incrementally from the precomputed Gram matrix. Take the best few discrete selections, break their symmetry gradually by first optimizing a small LogSumExp objective with all points free but adding tiny deterministic random displacements of sizes $10^{-3}$, $10^{-2}$, and $3\times10^{-2}$, then continue with ordinary Adam/L-BFGS annealing. Spend at most about 40 seconds on discrete selection, 90 seconds on continuous release, and reserve the remainder for LP polish, returning the incumbent immediately if any stage exceeds its budget.

idea: Contact-imbalance surgery that deletes low-contact outliers plus overloaded jammed points and regrows them in the largest spherical holes followed by Riesz-energy basin hopping and hinge/LSE/LP promotion.
Lift codes to S^8 for LogSumExp reorganization then flatten with increasing ninth-coordinate penalty and hinge-descent to a new 8D basin.
direction: Escape through a dimension-lifted continuation path. Embed the code in $\mathbb R^9$, initially by appending a zero coordinate and then optimizing 121 points on $S^8$ with a LogSumExp objective, where additional freedom should allow the contact topology to reorganize at a lower nine-dimensional maximum; run several lifts from the incumbent and from fresh random 9D codes. Then introduce a schedule $\lambda=0,10,30,100,300,1000$ penalizing $\lambda\sum_i z_i^2$, where $z_i$ is the ninth coordinate, interleaving penalty increases with smooth minimax optimization so the configuration flattens onto an 8D equator while retaining as much of the reorganized topology as possible. After projecting to $\mathbb R^8$ and renormalizing, continue with hinge-loss optimization at targets descending from the projected value toward $0.4595$, discard branches whose ninth-coordinate energy cannot be removed without exceeding roughly $0.462$, and reserve the final 25 seconds for trust-region LP polishing of the best flattened branch.

Stress-rebalanced weighted LogSumExp annealing with isotropy and max-balance penalties, void-reinsertion of high-residual/low- and high-degree points, and final LP polish.

idea: Overpopulate the record with hole-inserted points, rearrange the larger code, then greedily deflate back to 121 with Adam repair.
direction: Use overpopulation-and-deflation rather than deletion from 121: augment `best.npy` with 5–7 points placed in its largest spherical holes, optimise the resulting 126–128-point code with hinge loss at $t=0.460$ followed by LogSumExp annealing so the extra points force wholesale rearrangement, then delete one point at a time—choosing the point with the largest sum of $\max(0,\langle x_i,x_j\rangle-0.44)^2$ over neighbours—re-optimising for 150 cheap Adam steps after each deletion until 121 points remain. Repeat for three different hole-insertion seeds, keep only endpoints below 0.462 before LP, LP-polish the single best endpoint for at most 30 s, and compare against the incumbent; this “squeeze through $N>121$” path changes which points survive instead of trying to improve a fixed jammed set directly.

idea: Spatial cluster knockout with greedy hole refilling plus hinge and LogSumExp annealing and LP promotion.
direction: Perform large spatial cluster knockout surgery on `best.npy`: using a loose contact threshold of $10^{-4}$, select a seed point among the highest-degree points, remove it plus its 11–19 nearest neighbours by angle (not merely the globally worst points), freeze the remaining 102–109 points, and insert replacements greedily from 50,000 random sphere samples minimising the maximum cosine to the frozen set; then optimise only the inserted points with a hinge loss at target $t=0.455$ for 300 Adam steps, unfreeze all points for LogSumExp annealing ($\beta=100\to2000$, $\le$800 Adam/L-BFGS steps), and LP-polish only the best two outcomes for at most 15 s each. Run 6–10 knockouts of sizes 12, 16, and 20 within 150 s, reject any result whose contact graph at threshold $10^{-4}$ differs from the record by fewer than 50 edges, and return the best LP-polished survivor, falling back to `best.npy` if none beats it.

idea: Structured non-record search from E8/D8/product pools with greedy max-min selection, vectorised Adam LogSumExp screening, and single-seed L-BFGS plus LP promotion.
direction: Generate genuinely non-record basins from structured $R^8$ constructions and screen them cheaply before any LP: build candidate pools from the 240 $E_8$ roots $(\pm1,\pm1,0^6)/\sqrt2$ and permutations, $D_8$-type vectors, and product codes $(a u,b v)$ with $u,v\in S^3$ taken from 24-cell/16-cell/random $S^3$ codes and $a^2+b^2=1$ for $a\in\{0.5,1/\sqrt2,0.8\}$; from each pool greedily select 121 points by max-min cosine with 200 random restarts and local swaps, then run batched vectorised Adam LogSumExp optimisation ($\beta=50\to1000$, at most 1000 steps, no LP) on at least 32 such seeds. Promote only seeds reaching max cosine $<0.475$ and with contact-graph Hamming distance $>100$ from the record to a short L-BFGS anneal, and LP-polish only the single best promoted seed for $\le20$ s; hard-cap the screening phase at 90 s to avoid the previous symmetric-search timeout.

idea: De-novo random plus E8-greedy starts with staged LogSumExp L-BFGS annealing and LP trust-region polish, keeping lab best as fallback to escape the jammed basin.
Multi-basin LogSumExp annealing with Adam from perturbed, fresh and hole-regrown starts and greedy max-pair squeezing, keeping the best to guarantee no regression without costly LP.
Large spatial cluster knockout surgery with frozen-set greedy hole filling, subset hinge Adam and full LogSumExp annealing plus LP polish.
direction: Perform large spatial cluster knockout surgery on `best.npy`: using a loose contact threshold of $10^{-4}$, select a seed point among the highest-degree points, remove it plus its 11–19 nearest neighbours by angle (not merely the globally worst points), freeze the remaining 102–109 points, and insert replacements greedily from 50,000 random sphere samples minimising the maximum cosine to the frozen set; then optimise only the inserted points with a hinge loss at target $t=0.455$ for 300 Adam steps, unfreeze all points for LogSumExp annealing ($\beta=100\to2000$, $\le$800 Adam/L-BFGS steps), and LP-polish only the best two outcomes for at most 15 s each. Run 6–10 knockouts of sizes 12, 16, and 20 within 150 s, reject any result whose contact graph at threshold $10^{-4}$ differs from the record by fewer than 50 edges, and return the best LP-polished survivor, falling back to `best.npy` if none beats it.

idea: Overpopulate to 126-128 points in the largest holes to force rearrangement, then greedily deflate back to 121 by worst hinge-stress deletion.
direction: Use overpopulation-and-deflation rather than deletion from 121: augment `best.npy` with 5–7 points placed in its largest spherical holes, optimise the resulting 126–128-point code with hinge loss at $t=0.460$ followed by LogSumExp annealing so the extra points force wholesale rearrangement, then delete one point at a time—choosing the point with the largest sum of $\max(0,\langle x_i,x_j\rangle-0.44)^2$ over neighbours—re-optimising for 150 cheap Adam steps after each deletion until 121 points remain. Repeat for three different hole-insertion seeds, keep only endpoints below 0.462 before LP, LP-polish the single best endpoint for at most 30 s, and compare against the incumbent; this “squeeze through $N>121$” path changes which points survive instead of trying to improve a fixed jammed set directly.

idea: Structured non-record basin search from E8/D8/product pools with greedy max-min selection, batched Adam LogSumExp screening, Hamming-distinct promotion, and single-seed L-BFGS plus trust-region LP polish.
direction: Generate genuinely non-record basins from structured $R^8$ constructions and screen them cheaply before any LP: build candidate pools from the 240 $E_8$ roots $(\pm1,\pm1,0^6)/\sqrt2$ and permutations, $D_8$-type vectors, and product codes $(a u,b v)$ with $u,v\in S^3$ taken from 24-cell/16-cell/random $S^3$ codes and $a^2+b^2=1$ for $a\in\{0.5,1/\sqrt2,0.8\}$; from each pool greedily select 121 points by max-min cosine with 200 random restarts and local swaps, then run batched vectorised Adam LogSumExp optimisation ($\beta=50\to1000$, at most 1000 steps, no LP) on at least 32 such seeds. Promote only seeds reaching max cosine $<0.475$ and with contact-graph Hamming distance $>100$ from the record to a short L-BFGS anneal, and LP-polish only the single best promoted seed for $\le20$ s; hard-cap the screening phase at 90 s to avoid the previous symmetric-search timeout.

idea: Escape the jammed asymmetric basin with antipodal and 11-fold rotation symmetric subspace search plus large cap-knockout regrowth and staged LogSumExp annealing before a final LP squeeze.

Break the jammed 750-contact basin with large topology jumps — per-block random rotations, large 15-25 point cap knockouts with hole regrowth, and E8-root subset restarts — followed by hinge-feasibility plus LogSumExp annealing and sparse LP polishing.
